prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1078; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Claimant reports neck and lower back discomfort and was advised to seek medical evaluation. Claimant is not represented by counsel at this time.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes lower back strain with stiffness and limited range of motion when getting out of bed. Reports visit to urgent care, where muscle strain was diagnosed and a follow-up was recommended. Medical bills and treatment notes requested. Claimant has been advised of the process for submitting documentation directly.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles received from claimant. Damage to rear bumper and trunk area of claimant vehicle is consistent with reported impact. Repair estimate ordered from preferred shop. Rental car coverage explained to claimant, who has elected to use a rental while the vehicle is repaired.

Entry 4: Received physical therapy referral and initial treatment notes. Diagnosis remains soft tissue lumbar strain. Claimant reports pain is improving with therapy but still interferes with lifting and prolonged sitting. Claimant asked general questions about how injury claims are valued; explained that the adjuster cannot give legal advice and that claimant may consult an attorney if they wish.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant. Physical therapy continuing two times per week. Claimant reports improvement and no new symptoms. Repair estimate reviewed and approved. File remains open pending final medical records and therapy discharge summary. Next review scheduled for the coming weeks.
